cold_plate.source: Thesis group, IE_Thesis_Master_Document.pdf (2026-10-14): R = (T_cpu,max - T_in) / P_cpu from Wang et al. (2026), Fig. 10(a), CPU 1, at 200 W. Flow is chosen from these settings; 0.05 and 0.35 L/min are only the limits of Eq. (47); 0.264 L/min is only the pump reference flow of Eq. (48) (0.657 mW, Wang and Tao 2025).

time.convention: A_i = first period it may run; D_i = period by which it must be finished (CT_i = ST_i + ET_i <= D_i); AD_i = D_i - A_i - ET_base_i, Eq. (22) as an equality

work_rule: ET_is = W_i / (C_req_i * f_s * DPF * dt): a workload is served by its own requested cores, not the whole server. ET_base_i uses f_ref.
thermal_fit: steady state T_cpu = T_inlet + th_a_C + th_R_C_per_W * P_IT; per period T[t] = alpha*T[t-1] + (1-alpha)*steady, alpha = th_alpha_5min. Fitted from UniMelb; not part of the thesis formulation.

changes: B_i = 1 for the 4 workloads arriving in periods 3-5 (already running at the start, so they keep their server, Eq. 29)
availability.csv: server 3 has AV = 0 in periods 37-48 (one hour of maintenance, Eq. 11)
baseline_schedule.csv rebuilt with the least-loaded rule, which skips unavailable periods
derived_from.purpose: exercise Eq. (11) and (29), which are never binding in small/consolidated6/thesis10
